errors.text_span: The chart contains twelve distinct slices, representing twelve different news sources.
errors.evidence: The pie chart contains 18 distinct slices, not twelve.

errors.text_span: followed by “Shareblue” at approximately 13% and “Fox News” at approximately 13%.
errors.evidence: The slice with a value of 13 is labeled "Other", not "Shareblue" or "Fox News". The values for "Shareblue" and "Fox News" are both 3.
The dark green slice corresponds to "The Daily Caller". "Drudge Report" corresponds to the orange slice.
The value shown for the NPR slice is 6, not 8.

errors.text_span: “The Daily Caller,” “The Huffington Post”, “CNN,” “The Guardian,” “BBC,” “Vox,” ... and “Other,” with approximate proportions of 6%, 5%, 4%, 3%, 3%, 3%, ... and 3% respectively.
errors.evidence: This list assigns numerous incorrect values to the media outlets. For example: The Daily Caller is 8 (not 6), The Huffington Post is 7 (not 5), The Guardian is 5 (not 3), BBC is 4 (not 3), Vox is 6 (not 3), and Other is 13 (not 3).
There is no category named "Daily Mail State". The chart shows two separate categories, "Daily Mail" and "Red State", which each have a value of 3.

errors.text_span: The chart includes percentage labels within each slice
errors.evidence: The labels inside the slices are numbers (e.g., 14, 13, 8); the percentage symbol (%) is not actually displayed in the chart.

errors.text_span: all slices appear to be ordered from largest to smallest in terms of area
errors.evidence: The ordering is not strictly largest to smallest. The second largest slice, "Other" (13), is placed at the very end of the sequence, after all the smaller slices.
